themes.consensus_view: Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan all say AI demand for memory chips is strong and still outrunning supply, and none of them argues the other side.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks say AI is driving strong memory demand and keeping the tech/AI group fundamentally supported.
evidence_quotes: The company believes demand across the memory hierarchy accelerated once again in the quarter from AI
AI and HBM demand continues to outstrip supply
we still see the tech/AI complex being supported fundamentally

themes.consensus_view: Three banks flag French government finances and politics as a live risk, but none has staked a directional trade view on it yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Deutsche Bank, TS Lombard and Goldman Sachs all name French fiscal strain and political risk as a subject to watch, without taking a directional stance.

themes.consensus_view: Three desks flag the gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields as widening, but none has staked a directional view on where it goes next.

facts_agreed.claim: Deutsche Bank, The Market Ear and Goldman Sachs all cite the French-German government bond yield spread as widening.

themes.consensus_view: Both desks say stress in European bond and credit markets is building and is showing up more in credit and government bond prices than in stock indices.

facts_agreed.claim: Both banks describe rising stress in bond and credit markets, with Europe showing widening spreads.
evidence_quotes: the bond market stress continued, with the 10yr Treasury yield (+4.9bps) rising
iTraxx Main is showing considerably more stress than equities.

themes.consensus_view: Both banks covering this theme see demand for AI computing capacity continuing to grow, driven by limited supply and rising use of AI agents, and neither argues against it.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI compute and inference is rising and the market is short of capacity, which both banks treat as a positive for infrastructure.
evidence_quotes: millions of persistent agents doing work continuously, that is another powerful accelerator for inference
If compute keeps getting more valuable because there isn’t enough, it is very hard to be bearish

themes.consensus_view: Only Goldman Sachs staked a view here: it expects the Fed to skip an October rate hike and push the second hike to December, helped by August core inflation coming in well below expectations.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs now thinks an October Fed hike is unlikely and expects the second hike in December.
evidence_quotes: we now think that an October hike is unlikely.
